page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-64 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the n4 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel processor with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs, utilizing hyperthreading with two threads per core. The instance is configured with 256 GB of dedicated system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of a 48 KB L1d cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory and multi-core performance. The instance achieves a memory bandwidth of 4103.87 GB/sec for small-block read-only cached operations, and 277.75 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. Multi-core performance is highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 17690.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 67610.19, both placing in the top 25% tier. The processor's support for advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), is reflected in strong results for extended instructions (72759.95) and encryption (57650.04) on Passmark. Single-core performance, such as the stress-ng single-core score of 1689.08 and Geekbench single-core score of 1777.0, remains in the middle 50% tier.

The n4-standard-64 demonstrates high throughput in database and web serving workloads, achieving 70.46 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 86.82 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. It also shows strong capabilities in software compilation (41502.0 on Geekbench) and prompt processing for large language models, handling 229.23 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. However, text generation for larger 70B models is limited to an average speed of 3.7 tokens/sec. Given its high resource density and strong multi-core efficiency without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware, this instance is suited for multi-threaded enterprise applications, database operations, software build pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
